description: We are a motivated team joining NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 – Irbid. We love software, AI, data analysis, web development, and space. We seek committed teammates to share ideas, solve problems, and build a creative solution using NASA’s open data. Skills in programming, AI/ML, data, UI/UX, design, research, storytelling, and presenting are welcome.
summary:
OUTPOST ONE is a browser-based lunar outpost simulation that trains junior astronauts to think like mission engineers. Players run a Moon outpost across eight objectives, managing limited resources where every decision has consequences and trade-offs. This addresses the challenge that space-themed STEM content often oversimplifies real engineering choices: instead of one right answer, players must balance competing needs under pressure.

The game is built with React and Three.js and includes a 3D lunar environment, rover and relay interactions, storms and engineering events, three difficulty levels (Easy, Normal and Hard), and a mission report that rates decisions and learning. Ten science topics, each linked to NASA references, explain concepts such as space weather, radiation and life support, with four optional questions and feedback. A rule-based Mission Advisor (not an AI model) gives players guidance. An archived NASA DONKI solar-flare reference connects gameplay to real space weather. All resource values and outcomes are simulated for education and are not live NASA measurements.
details:
OUTPOST ONE (team StarBound) is an interactive lunar outpost simulation that lets players experience the engineering trade-offs behind a real Moon mission. Instead of one correct answer, players manage limited resources across eight mission objectives, respond to storms and engineering events, and see the consequences of every decision.

How it works: the player commands a lunar outpost in a 3D environment, operating a rover and relay, managing critical resources, and completing objectives. Each objective ends with a completion card that explains the science behind it, and four optional questions give feedback. A mission report at the end rates the player's decisions and shows learning statistics. Three difficulty levels (Easy, Normal and Hard) change the challenge, and difficulty balance was checked with seeded simulation campaigns.

Educational content: ten science topics covering space weather, radiation, life support and engineering challenges, each linked to NASA references. The game clearly separates real scientific concepts, simplified educational explanations, and simulated gameplay data, which are not live NASA measurements. An archived NASA DONKI solar-flare reference connects the gameplay to real space weather. The in-game Mission Advisor is rule-based (programmed rules, not an AI model).

Tools: React, Three.js, TypeScript, built with Replit Agent and deployed on Netlify. TypeScript type checking, production build verification and regression checks were used for quality assurance.

Impact: the project helps young learners understand that real space missions are about balancing competing needs under constraints, not simple right-or-wrong choices.

Play the game: https://boisterous-rugelach-a2db28.netlify.app

Source code and documentation: https://github.com/Osama-ahmad1/outpost-one
